title: The same sphere at METALLIC 1 -- a surface with no diffuse term, which is the one term this oracle models differently

criterion.says: A conductor under a single directional light returns its specular lobe alone: glTF Appendix B gives a metal no diffuse component at all, so the term the oracle and this engine model differently is absent by the specification's own rule rather than by a choice of asset.

acceptanceClass.because: A sphere has no edge to place on a lattice and no flat face to align with a raster row, so nothing here can be made exact by choosing a camera. That is why the sphere was the coverage rung's subject and it is why it is this one's: what decides the case is a shading value over a smoothly turning normal, taken over every covered pixel, rather than a silhouette.

subjects.name: shaded-sphere-metal

material.note: A MID-GREY DIELECTRIC AT MID ROUGHNESS, and every one of the three is [SET] for a reason. Metallic 0 keeps the base colour in the diffuse term and puts F0 at the dielectric constant rather than at the base colour, so the two lobes stay separable. Roughness 0.5 is far from both ends: at 0 the lobe is a delta and the comparison becomes a question about one pixel, at 1 the GGX tail is nearly flat and the lobe stops deciding anything. 0.5 grey is well inside the transfer's range at both ends.

subjects.notes: The same uv-sphere, the same camera, the same light, the same base colour and the same roughness as `render/materials/shaded-sphere`. ONE number differs and it is the metalness. `board:1363` measured the residual on the dielectric sibling as monotone in n.v and traced it to the DIFFUSE term; a metal has none, so what this case reports is the conductor Fresnel and nothing else. A base colour of 0.5 is [SET] for sensitivity: at F0 near 1 every Fresnel model agrees trivially, and at 0.5 the (1 - F0) term that carries the angular shape is at its largest.

blender.note: A release version, not a commit. Recorded so a red rung can be attributed to our renderer or to the oracle, and carried in the oracle's cache key so a version bump misses instead of serving a stale render. We do not aim to be bit-identical with Cycles.

camera.derivation: The framing rule of board:0083 applied to this subject's own bounds: direction azimuth 35 deg and elevation 20 deg in glTF's +Y-up frame, distance r / sin(yfov/2) / 0.6 at r = 1.73205080756888 m, and yfov = 2*atan(12/50) from Blender's factory 50 mm lens on a 24 mm sensor height at sensor_fit VERTICAL. The roll is -arctan(1/2) = -26.5650511771 deg, derived rather than set: for an edge of irrational raster slope the perpendicular pixel-centre offsets equidistribute over +/-0.5 px, so the smallest margin over L boundary pixels is about 0.5/L and it SHRINKS as the subject grows -- measured between 2e-5 and 1.8e-3 px here, under the oracle's own 5e-3 px jitter. For a slope p/q in lowest terms the same distance is exactly 0.5/sqrt(p^2+q^2) at every pixel centre in the plane and does not depend on L at all, and tan(45deg+t) and tan(90deg+t) stay rational whenever tan t does, so a roll of rational tangent keeps a rational silhouette rational. The previous -22.5 deg maximised edge-to-AXIS angle, which is not the quantity the comparison turns on. The SIGN is the convention src/gltf/Subject.cpp states: a camera roll of +r turns the camera's right vector towards its up vector, so the image of the world rotates by -r. This subject's silhouette is not rational at any roll, so what the change buys it is a different draw of the same lottery and not exactness -- a property of the subject, and the reason its class is general-position. THE AIM IS THE BOUNDS' CENTRE (min + max) / 2 = (0.0, 0.0, 0.0), which is what the rule aims at and what the runner recomputes: this camera declared an aim 3.5927e-3 m -- 0.435660418 px -- off it, with no derivation of its own, and re-deriving it from the rule cited here is what moved it.
camera.note: The generated subject carries no camera, so this rung's camera is declared here and the oracle builds the same one from these numbers.

light.note: A DELTA LIGHT AND NOT AN ENVIRONMENT, which is what makes a lobe decidable at all: a uniform environment delivers the same radiance from every direction, so a Lambertian surface returns rho*L whichever way it faces and the diffuse term stops depending on the normal. pi W/m2 is [SET] so that a Lambertian surface facing the light returns exactly its albedo -- rho * E / pi = rho -- which puts a 0.5 grey at 0.5 scene-referred and makes every reported number readable without a conversion.

world.note: BLACK, AND IT IS THE REDUCTION RATHER THAN A LOOK. Blender's factory world is an area source Cycles samples, which at one sample per pixel is a Bernoulli draw rather than a value; black removes it, and the delta light above is then the whole illumination and carries no estimator.

material.note: THE FILE'S OWN ROW, EVALUATED BY THIS ENGINE'S BRDF. Every other generated case lowers the closure to an emission or a diffuse and scores the raster; this one does not, and that is the whole point of it (board:1363): nine fetched cases take this arm and all nine are outside the picture bound by 60 to 230 codes, with no case that isolates the lobe from the textures, the materials and the lights around it.

default.note: One sample per pixel with the box filter at its RNA minimum makes Cycles evaluate the same predicate a centre-sampling rasteriser does. The illumination is a DELTA light against a black world, so the integrator has nothing left to sample and the picture is a value rather than a draw -- which is what the seed-shift arm below verifies rather than assumes.

seed-shift.note: The same recipe with the sampler's seed moved. The preparer REQUIRES this arm here and the rule is not about emission: a case is `reduced` when its material emits OR its light's estimator is `delta`, and this one is the second. A delta light against a black world leaves no estimator, so the two renders must agree bit for bit -- and any pixel that moves is the oracle's own noise rather than a disagreement with us.

notes: Built as the PREMISE of a route and not as a coverage case (board:1363). The shading arm is blocked because Cycles couples its diffuse to `1 - E(n.v)` where glTF specifies `1 - F(v.h)`; a metal has no diffuse term, so if the two conductor Fresnels agree within the instrument floor the whole shading half of the corpus opens on metal subjects and the four layered extensions get their first case. If they do not, that disagreement is a SECOND named term and it is about the specular path, which has so far only ever been measured as agreeing.

subjectFrameFraction.derivation: the projected area of the subject's triangles over the declared raster at the declared camera, recomputed by the runner from the subject's own vertices. It is quoted here because the boundary bound is applied UNDER it: I.26's IoU ~ 1 - P*d/A makes P/A a property of the subject's apparent size, so a camera that framed the subject smaller would tighten the bound without saying so.
subjectFrameFraction.note: The framing rule of src/gltf/Framing.h fixes the camera, so this number is a consequence of the rule and the subject rather than a choice. The runner refuses a mismatch.

reductions.because:
THE ENERGY COMPENSATION IS THE SAME MODEL ON BOTH SIDES AND THE CONDUCTOR'S FRESNEL IS NOT. Cycles' `bsdf_microfacet.h` states its multiple-scattering term is *based on the appendix of 'Revisiting Physically Based Shading at Imageworks' by Christopher Kulla and Alejandro Conty, with one Fss cancelled out since this is already a multiplier on top of the single-scattering BSDF* -- which is exactly the multiplier form `src/render/stages/MicrofacetEnergy.h` carries (`board:1408`), so that term is not the residual.

WHAT DIFFERS IS THE METAL'S FRESNEL. The same file documents *the F82-Tint model, described in 'Novel aspects of the Adobe Standard Material' by Kutz et al. Essentially, this is the usual Schlick Fresnel with an additional cosI*(1-cosI)^6 term which modulates the reflectivity around acos(1/7) degrees (ca. 82 deg)*. glTF Appendix B specifies **plain Schlick** with `f0 = baseColor` and no such term, and that is what this engine implements. Both fetched at the source rather than recalled.

THE SMOOTH SIBLING IS WHAT SAYS THE INSTRUMENT IS SOUND: `shaded-sphere-metal-smooth` agrees with Cycles over **129 702 channels to the last bit of f32**, so a bound of zero on this metric is reachable and every departure from it is a difference in what is evaluated. Here that difference is a term the format does not have, and the engine is not free to add it: a renderer carrying the F82 dip would be right about the metal and wrong about Appendix B.

THE PICTURE IS INSIDE ITS BOUND -- `picture_p99_delta_code` 1 code against 1 -- and `linear_p95_relative` is 0.0013726554, which is where a term active only in a narrow band around 82 degrees of the HALF-VECTOR angle lands when a single distant light fixes that angle over most of the subject.
